speaker: ORB
text: Helmets off. Breathe. That air is the only thing on this rock I'm handing out for free.

speaker: ORB
text: Meet Pip. Meet Gruff. Four years they were a band — one bus, one stage, one van that smelled like a drum kit. Then she went solo. He found out from a poster.

speaker: ORB
text: Thirty days on a planet one kilometre across. Nobody leaves the rock. Nobody leaves the other one. Survive that, together, and this crate goes home with them.

speaker: ORB
text: When did the band end?

speaker: PIP
text: Three years back.

speaker: GRUFF
text: She ended it. Halfway through a tour.

speaker: ORB
text: Still sore, then.

speaker: ORB
text: Nobody's dragging you into this. But the moment those anklets close, the thirty days are counting — and nothing I say afterwards can un-count them.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Counting.

speaker: ORB
text: Both locked.

speaker: ORB
text: See this ring? Step across it and you've quit. If one of you quits, both of you fly home tonight, and the crate flies home with me. There is no version where one of you crosses and the other one wins. The ring is the only exit on this rock, and it's an exit for two.

speaker: ORB
text: Enjoy the view. There's more of it than you'd think. And a little less every time I visit.

speaker: ORB
text: One thousand metres across. Its own thin sky, its own sad little sunrise every six hours. North pole: Pip's camp. A tent, a kettle, and a keyboard she has not touched since she landed.

speaker: ORB
text: South pole: Gruff's cave. A mattress, and a wall he has already introduced himself to. On a world this size, they can go a week without crossing paths. In some households, that is the whole arrangement.

speaker: ORB
text: That is The Count. It keeps the day and it keeps the diameter. It does not negotiate, it does not blink, and it has never once been right about a landing.

speaker: ORB
text: The tether. Forty metres of braided gravity. It stretches; it does not break. I tested it on a moon.

speaker: ORB
text: And on the equator — a crate. Not the prize. Something else. It stays shut until I say, and I am not going to say for a long, long while.

speaker: ORB
text: The bathroom. It's a hole. The hole has a view.

speaker: PIP
text: You are not serious. There isn't even a door.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Best seat on the planet. I'm not sharing it.

speaker: PIP
text: Forty metres of tether says you are.

speaker: PIP
text: We're going to have to talk about it. Not today. But it's coming, and I honestly don't know which one of us cracks first.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I've been cold to her. I'm entitled to that. I didn't leave. She did. Everybody keeps forgetting that part.

speaker: ORB
text: They think this is a show about surviving.

speaker: ORB
text: It isn't.

speaker: ORB
text: It's about whether two people who broke each other once can stand on a rock the size of a car and not do it twice.

speaker: ORB
text: Day two. Two sunrises, two hemispheres, zero conversation. So let me explain the engine, because everything that follows runs on it.

speaker: ORB
text: Nine numbers on that ladder. They will hear every one of them out loud, and they will see every one of them on The Count, and not one of them goes back up. Every deal I offer them makes this planet smaller. Right now they can avoid each other. At a hundred metres, they'll hear each other breathe. At two metres there is nowhere left to stand except together — and I mean that as geometry, not poetry.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Quiet. I could get used to quiet. Nobody singing in the next room. Nobody singing at all. Just me, a rock, and a wall that doesn't argue back.

speaker: PIP
text: He's fine. He's always fine. That was the whole problem — you cannot fight a wall, and you cannot leave one, either. So I did the second thing. Three years later, here I am on a rock with the wall, and the wall got a cave.

speaker: ORB
text: So here is what the next twenty-eight days answer. Does a smaller world pull two people back together — or does it finish the job they started?

speaker: ORB
text: Midnight. Which means me. Every five days I visit, and every visit comes with a choice. Two platters. Under the first: you keep your thousand-metre planet exactly as it is. Under the second: you halve it — and I add a hundred thousand to whatever's in that crate.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Money is money. I've slept in worse places than half a planet.

speaker: PIP
text: Of course he'll take it. He'd take anything shiny. That's the drummer in him — hit the thing that makes the noise.

speaker: ORB
text: Two rules on every visit. One: you answer together, or you don't answer. Two: The Count goes once around the pad, and when it gets back I need a word. One word. Silence counts as keeping the planet, which is the only free thing I've ever offered.

speaker: GRUFF
text: You do the honours. You're good at leaving things behind.

speaker: PIP
text: Say that again and I'll keep the planet just to spite you.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Then keep it. Half a planet's still a planet. I'm not the one who needs the money to prove something.

speaker: PIP
text: Halve it.

speaker: ORB
text: Then look up.

speaker: ORB
text: A wedge, sheared clean. Their first camp is on it. Nobody gets that back — not for a hundred thousand, not for anything. Watch it go. It's the first thing on this rock they lost together, and it will not be the last.

speaker: GRUFF
text: My mattress was on that.

speaker: ORB
text: Day five. Five hundred metres. A hundred thousand richer and one hemisphere poorer. That is what a deal costs here — and it is the cheapest one I will ever offer.

speaker: ORB
text: Less than one day at half size, and the bill has arrived. Gravity rearranged itself while they slept. Both camps are sliding into the same valley, and neither of them packed for company.

speaker: ORB
text: That is Gruff. Snoring. It now carries across the entire planet, because there is no longer an entire planet. On day one she was five hundred metres from that noise. Tonight, forty. Tomorrow, the maths gets worse.

speaker: PIP
text: If I hold his nose for one minute, do I win the crate by myself? I'm asking for a friend. The friend is me.

speaker: PIP
text: Ow. Ow, ow. That is a floor made of planet.

speaker: GRUFF
text: …Pip? Is it the money or is it the snoring?

speaker: PIP
text: Go back to sleep. It's both.

speaker: ORB
text: Tally six. Scratched into the rock with a piece of the rock. Twenty-four to go.

speaker: PIP
text: I would rather be roped to somebody I'd never met. Somebody I'd never met would at least pretend to be interested in what I'm saying.

speaker: GRUFF
text: You'd rather be anywhere I'm not. You proved it with a tour bus and a head start. Don't act like it's news.

speaker: PIP
text: One song, Gruff. Four years, and you brought one song to the band. I wrote the other thirty in a van you were asleep in.

speaker: GRUFF
text: And you put your name on all thirty-one. Solo. So which of us actually left?

speaker: PIP
text: I wrote them! Writing them is the part that counts!

speaker: GRUFF
text: Then you didn't need a band. Good. You've got what you wanted. It's just smaller than you thought.

speaker: ORB
text: Remember this argument. In twenty-two days they'll be standing on a rock too small to have it on.

speaker: PIP
text: He's not wrong. That's the part I can't stand. I've had three years of being right about him, and he undid it in one sentence.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I said the thing I promised myself I would never say to her. Took me six days. That's a personal best.

speaker: ORB
text: Day seven. The first fight took eleven minutes. The silence after it took four hours.

speaker: PIP
text: Half?

speaker: GRUFF
text: …Half.

speaker: PIP
text: Start over. Just for the rock. Nothing from before comes up here unless we both say so.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Just for the rock.

speaker: ORB
text: That's a truce. It will last exactly until I come back — which, for the record, is in three days.

speaker: ORB
text: Midnight again. No platters tonight. Tonight's shrink is a gift, and gifts don't come with lids.

speaker: GRUFF
text: A gift.

speaker: PIP
text: Since when does a gift take something away from you? Every one of his gifts has a lid, and the lid has a price under it.

speaker: ORB
text: Since always. Look up.

speaker: ORB
text: Three hundred metres. Ten days ago they could lose each other for a week. Now the far side of the world is a four-minute walk. And a present for the house: The Count grew thrusters. It can fetch now. Ask it nicely — it will not understand a word, but it appreciates the tone.

speaker: ORB
text: One more thing before I go. So far the money has been polite. From tonight, it gets rude. And every time the money gets rude, so does the planet.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Looking forward to it. Nothing else to do up here.

speaker: PIP
text: He says that like it's a joke. It isn't. He'd sell the rock out from under us for a bath.

speaker: ORB
text: Left on a mattress at dawn: a moon rock, worked into a heart with what I assume was another moon rock. He doesn't mention it. She notices he didn't throw it in the hole.

speaker: ORB
text: Night ten. Three hundred metres, one fire that isn't a fire. I'm going to ask the thing I've wanted to ask since the helmets came off, and then I'm going to be quiet, which I'm told I'm bad at.

speaker: ORB
text: What actually broke the band?

speaker: PIP
text: Every night, in every dressing room, I'd sit there thinking: if I stood up and walked out right now, would anyone in this band notice before the encore? And I never got an answer, because I never tested it. So one night I tested it. I walked out before anybody could answer.

speaker: ORB
text: Hold onto what she just said. In fifteen days a light is going to check it.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I'd have noticed. I did notice. I noticed for about three years straight. I just never said it anywhere you could hear it.

speaker: PIP
text: You could have called. There's a phone in every van.

speaker: GRUFF
text: You'd changed the number. I checked. Twice. Second time I got a dentist in another city. Nice man. Didn't know you.

speaker: PIP
text: So what happens now?

speaker: GRUFF
text: Now we survive a rock. The rest of it can wait until the rock is smaller.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Two weeks. The furthest thing I've looked at in two weeks is thirty metres away, and it's her tent.

speaker: ORB
text: Day fourteen. He decides to walk it off. One lap of the world. He passes the crate. He passes the vent. He passes the crate again — which is the trouble with laps. On a normal planet you can walk until the problem is behind you. On this one the problem is forty seconds ahead of you, and it's the same crate.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I'm not doing great. Up here. The rock's holding up fine. I'm the one coming apart.

speaker: ORB
text: Day fifteen. Halfway. So I brought the best thing I own. A dome. Glass. A garden in it — real air, real trees, a real bath with real hot water. It's yours tonight. Sleep under glass, wake up to birdsong — I have birdsong. All it costs is the planet: three hundred metres, down to one hundred. At a hundred metres you will hear each other breathe. I did mention that.

speaker: GRUFF
text: There's a tree. There is an actual tree. I forgot what they look like from underneath.

speaker: PIP
text: No.

speaker: ORB
text: She gets ten seconds to change her mind.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Pip. There's a bath.

speaker: PIP
text: I said no. He keeps calling it the best thing he owns. Not the best thing we can win — the best thing he owns. That's a different sentence, and I don't like where it goes. Besides, a hundred metres is where he starts hearing me breathe. I'm not ready for him to hear me breathe.

speaker: ORB
text: Time. Dome's gone. Planet stays.

speaker: GRUFF
text: There were trees. I'd have given a whole planet for one tree. She didn't even look.

speaker: ORB
text: Any second thoughts? Sit with those for a while. And while you're sitting — the crate's still there. Still sealed. Still waiting on the right night.

speaker: ORB
text: Day sixteen. Ration bars, arranged into a heart, by the person who said no to a bath.

speaker: PIP
text: It's not a heart. It's a triangle that went wrong on the left.

speaker: GRUFF
text: It's a heart. I've drawn worse ones on drum cases. Yours has a corner. Mine had wheels.

speaker: PIP
text: So we're — what, then? Colleagues?

speaker: GRUFF
text: Bandmates. Say the real word.

speaker: PIP
text: …Bandmates.

speaker: ORB
text: Four notes on a ration tin. Keep those. They come back.

speaker: ORB
text: Alone, he reads. The title, in case you can't see it from there: How To Stop Being A Drummer About It. Chapter one is called "Listen." He takes notes. In pencil. Hard enough to go through the page.

speaker: GRUFF
text: "Before you hit something, ask what it did." …That's the whole chapter? Fine. Fine. I'll ask.

speaker: PIP
text: That thing is still on your head? Every photo we ever took, it was on your head. You slept in it.

speaker: GRUFF
text: There's a story behind it. You'll get it on the last night we're on this rock. Not one night sooner.

speaker: PIP
text: The last night. Why the last night?

speaker: GRUFF
text: Because on the last night you can't leave early.

speaker: PIP
text: He said the last night. So now I have to be here for the last night. He knows exactly what he did.

speaker: ORB
text: And that, for anyone taking notes, is how you keep somebody on a planet.

speaker: ORB
text: Day twenty. Tonight the crate can open. Five platters, revealed right to left — each one a price for the lid. And a warning, which I will only give once: the best deal on this tray may be the one you never lift.

speaker: ORB
text: Platter one. Open the crate for two hundred thousand out of the prize.

speaker: GRUFF
text: No.

speaker: ORB
text: Platter two. Half a million out of the prize.

speaker: PIP
text: Absolutely not. That's most of it.

speaker: ORB
text: Platter three. Open the crate — and the planet drops to twenty-five metres. The size of a house.

speaker: ORB
text: Five seconds on this one. Houses go fast.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Take it. A house is fine. I've lived in a house. Never lived in a planet.

speaker: PIP
text: Take it. Now — before I think about it.

speaker: ORB
text: Settled on three. Then let's see what you left on the tray.

speaker: ORB
text: Free. Platter four was free.

speaker: GRUFF
text: You said the best deal might be the one—

speaker: ORB
text: I did. I said it out loud, with my halo on. Look up.

speaker: ORB
text: Twenty-five metres. A planet the size of a house, bought at a price they didn't have to pay. Every deal costs something here — and the free ones cost the most, because you remember them.

speaker: ORB
text: Two tickets on the rescue ship. One each. Whoever wins whatever's in the prize, whoever doesn't — you both leave this rock alive, and you both leave it on the same ship.

speaker: PIP
text: Two names. He put both names on. I didn't think there'd be two names.

speaker: GRUFF
text: That's it. That's the thing I came up here for. Not the money — that. Her name on a ticket next to mine.

speaker: ORB
text: The tickets have a price. It's underneath you. Look down.

speaker: ORB
text: Twenty-five metres. From orbit it looks like a pebble somebody dropped two people on. Arm's reach is now the entire neighbourhood. Sleeping, washing, the hole with a view — all of it within three metres of the other person, for as long as there is a planet.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I can hear you swallow. I can hear you think. I'm going to learn what your thoughts sound like, and neither of us wants that.

speaker: PIP
text: There is no smaller than this.

speaker: ORB
text: There are five smaller than this. I've counted.

speaker: ORB
text: Rules change. Right now. All of them.

speaker: ORB
text: This is the launch key. It fits that pod. The pod has one seat. Turn the key, and you leave tonight — with everything in the crate, and everything I've added to it. The one still standing on the rock gets nothing. Not a ticket. Not a ride. Nothing.

speaker: PIP
text: One seat.

speaker: GRUFF
text: One seat.

speaker: ORB
text: I'll say the rest once, so nobody argues later. The key stays on the platter, on the pad, inside the red ring — where either of you can reach it and neither of you can pretend you couldn't. The red line still means quit: cross it, both of you go home empty. The key means the opposite. One of you goes home full.

speaker: PIP
text: He put it inside the ring. Right where we'd have to look at it every time we look at anything.

speaker: ORB
text: And from tonight the planet loses size every single day. Twenty metres. Twelve. Seven. Four. Two. Five days, five numbers, one key. The red line still quits you both. The key only quits one.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Two metres. That's a doormat.

speaker: ORB
text: That's the whole idea.

speaker: ORB
text: Here is my favourite hour of the month. That column hears everything — pulse, breath, the little pause before a lie. Stand in it, answer a question. Green means true. Red means you lied to somebody you're tethered to — and the tether will remember. One question each. Choose it like it's the last thing you'll ever find out about the other one.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I'll go. Before I lose my nerve. I've had a question for three years; might as well ask it under a light.

speaker: ORB
text: Pip. Into the beam. He asks, you answer.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Were you better off solo?

speaker: PIP
text: No.

speaker: ORB
text: True.

speaker: GRUFF
text: …You sold twice what we sold.

speaker: PIP
text: I said better off. I didn't say richer. Different question. Ask me the other one.

speaker: PIP
text: Would you turn the key?

speaker: GRUFF
text: I would never leave you on a rock.

speaker: ORB
text: The Count carries the beam. The Count has chosen this exact moment to fall over. We'll call that answer… unread.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Fix it. Ask me again.

speaker: ORB
text: One question per person. That was yours.

speaker: PIP
text: Ask me. Ask me the same thing. I'll stand in it all day.

speaker: ORB
text: Would you turn the key?

speaker: PIP
text: No.

speaker: ORB
text: One green. One blank. Hers is verified. His is a machine that fell over. Five days from that blank, we find out what colour it was — and the only instrument left that can tell us is a lever.

speaker: GRUFF
text: It was true. I don't need a light to tell me what I meant. …Mostly true. The light would have said mostly.

speaker: PIP
text: I believe him. I do. But I believed him about a lot of things, and I've got a light that says the machine wasn't sure.

speaker: GRUFF
text: She got her ending. Tickets, tears, the arm round the shoulder, the whole thing, on camera. That's hers now. Nobody can take it off her.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I could turn this and be halfway home before she wakes up. The whole crate. And not one person watching would call it wrong — she did it first. She just didn't have a key.

speaker: GRUFF
text: …Not tonight.

speaker: ORB
text: Day twenty-six. Twelve metres. Two soundproof pods, because at this size a closed door is the only privacy left, and I'm feeling generous.

speaker: PIP
text: Maybe he wants it even. I took the band, he takes the crate — maybe that's fair, and I'm the only one who doesn't see it. He still hasn't told me about the goggle. He said the last night. The last night is three nights away, and I don't know if he'll be here for it.

speaker: ORB
text: You're not planning to launch alone, are you?

speaker: GRUFF
text: …Ask me on the last night. Everything's on the last night. It's getting crowded.

speaker: PIP
text: I can see his mouth move. I can't hear a word. That's the band, actually. That was the whole band.

speaker: ORB
text: He didn't say no. I've been doing this a long time. They always say no.

speaker: ORB
text: Day twenty-seven. Seven metres. Walking is now a three-legged race where the third leg is the planet.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Left. Your left. That's my left.

speaker: PIP
text: There's only one left on a rock this size, Gruff, and you're standing on it.

speaker: ORB
text: Day twenty-eight. Four metres. He's taller than the world now. She fits inside his shadow. Somewhere under all that fur is a hand, and the hand is on a lever.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Every time she bumps me I want to pull this. Every single time. And she bumps me about once a minute now, because there's nowhere else to be.

speaker: PIP
text: I think he's getting ready to go. Tonight, or tomorrow. I keep waking up and checking his side of the rock — and there isn't a his side any more. There's just the rock.

speaker: ORB
text: Two days. One key. Four metres of planet, going on two. And a clock you can't see yet — you can only hear it.

speaker: ORB
text: Day twenty-nine. Two metres. The last night. A clock goes into the rock: twenty-four hours, and it only runs one way.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I sold the van. The tour van. Three weeks before you left. I was buying you a solo record — a real one, a real label, your name on the sleeve. I was going to hand it to you on stage, last night of the tour, in front of everyone, so you'd know the band wanted it for you.

speaker: GRUFF
text: You left the week before I could. So I had a van's worth of money, a record with your name on it, and no you. This was the only thing from the band I didn't sell. I wear it so I'd remember I was going to do something good, once.

speaker: PIP
text: You sold the van for me.

speaker: GRUFF
text: It was a bad van. Smelled like a drum kit. You said so yourself, every morning for four years.

speaker: PIP
text: Three years I've thought he hated me for leaving. He didn't hate me for leaving. He hated that I left a week early. One week. I've been wrong about the whole shape of it.

speaker: ORB
text: Twenty-three hours, fifty minutes. The clock doesn't care what they just learned.

speaker: ORB
text: Eleven hours, seven minutes. Two shapes asleep against a crate, on a rock you could park in a driveway. One of them is not actually asleep. I'll let you work out which.

speaker: PIP
text: I'm scared of tomorrow. More scared of the next eleven hours than of the twenty-nine days before them. He's asleep. His hand is closer to the door than it is to me.

speaker: GRUFF
text: All of it would change my life. Half of it would change it less. And once we're off this rock, there's every chance we never speak again anyway.

speaker: ORB
text: Three seconds. That is where this ends up. Rewind ten minutes and watch how it gets there.

speaker: ORB
text: Ten minutes. The key still fits. The seat is still empty. Nobody has crossed the red line, and nobody has turned the key. Both of those are still available, and I am going to stand here and say the numbers out loud, because that's the job.

speaker: PIP
text: You said you'd never leave me on a rock.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I know what I said. The machine didn't.

speaker: ORB
text: One minute, ten seconds. Last call for the pod. After this, the key is a souvenir.

speaker: ORB
text: Fourteen seconds.

speaker: GRUFF
text: …Not for money. Not for a van. Not for anything with a lid on it.

speaker: PIP
text: Stay.

speaker: ORB
text: Three. Two. One.

speaker: ORB
text: Out of time.

speaker: ORB
text: And that is the sound of a rescue ship arriving at a world you could fit in a garage. Thirty days. Nine numbers. One key, never turned. Both tickets valid. Both seats taken.

speaker: ORB
text: Anklets open. Half each — and both tickets. So. Where do a singer and a drummer go from here?

speaker: ORB
text: I did not have that on my list of outcomes.

speaker: PIP
text: Tour van's sold. We'll need a new van.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I'll drum on the tin until we do.

speaker: ORB
text: The band is back. Subscribe.
